newsitem.title: USA: Slim margin of Florida voters back school tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Slim margin of Florida voters back school tax plan.

text.p: A bare majority of Florida voters support expanding the utility gross receipts tax to raise money for school construction, according to a poll released Tuesday.
Fifty-one percent of respondents in the Florida Voter survey said they supported the new tax for schools, 45 percent opposed it and four percent were undecided.
"Although a slim majority supports this proposed utility tax, it hardly demonstrates a clear mandate for it," said Jim Kane, chief pollster for the Florida Voter.
Florida already levies a 2.5 percent tax on telephone, electric and gas utility bills, raising $600 million annually to back Florida Board of Education Bonds for school building.

Gov. Lawton Chiles asked the legislature to expand the 2.5 percent tax to water, sewer, garbage collection and cable TV bills, phasing it in over five years. That would raise $179 million a year, enough to issue $1.3 million of new bonds.

The Florida Voter is an independent, nonpartisan, subscriber-supported publication that analyzes results of bi-monthly surveys of registered voters. The latest poll was conducted in telephone surveys of 605 registered Florida voters March 5-14 and has an error margin of four percent.
Voters with children in public schools favored the tax expansion by a margin of nearly 2-1, while voters without children in public schools were almost evenly divided.
"Quite frankly, we expected to see greater support from parents," Kane said.

Seventy percent of those surveyed said they believe Florida's public schools are somewhat or seriously overcrowded. But 75 percent completely or mostly agreed that the Florida Lottery should provide more than enough money for current public education needs.
"Many voters are not yet convinced that we have adequately exhausted existing revenue sources for education," Kane said.
